tasks.short: Check new applicants in Recruitee against the hard requirements and pass the suitable ones to the hiring manager.

today.trigger: New applications arrive in Recruitee for an open vacancy, checked in a batch two or three times a week.
steps: Open each new candidate in Recruitee and read the CV and motivation
Check the hard requirements: driving licence C/CE and code 95, forklift or VCA certificate, shift availability, work permit
Move suitable candidates to the 'Referred' stage and others to rejection
Email or Teams the hiring manager or site lead with a short list
Chase the manager when candidates sit unreviewed
drudgery: Reading CVs to find the same five certificates and licences
Retyping candidate summaries into emails for site leads
today.time_sinks: Peak-season volume for warehouse roles and CVs in mixed formats; candidates wait days while the batch builds up.

lenses.faster: A rules check pulls licences, certificates and availability from the application form and CV into fields, so the administrator reviews a pre-sorted list with a short summary per candidate instead of reading every CV; about a third of the time goes.
lenses.autonomous: A new application starts the extraction and the knock-out check; the administrator confirms each referral or rejection before the stage changes in Recruitee.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: applicants for driver and warehouse roles get a referral decision the same working day instead of at the next batch, which matters most in peak season when candidates take the first offer; demand would grow because site leads would open more vacancies in Recruitee instead of going straight to agencies.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses hunting for the forklift certificate in a two-page CV; the administrator wants more time on calling borderline candidates and on talking with site leads about what they actually need.
lenses.options: Little value in several drafts; the decision is pass or hold per candidate against fixed requirements.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from sorting CVs to keeping the requirement profiles per role correct with the recruiters and handling the doubtful cases; the job becomes slightly more expert because the administrator owns which requirements are hard knock-outs.
reach: Recruiter: first phone screen of warehouse and driver candidates; needs interview technique and knowledge of the roles
Recruiter: maintaining requirement profiles per vacancy in Recruitee; needs CAO function-level knowledge

tasks.human_edge: Judging candidates who do not fit the template, such as an experienced driver whose code 95 is being renewed or a career changer, and keeping the selection fair and explainable; the person owns the decision under GDPR Art. 22.
tasks.pattern_why: Applicant selection is a decision about people that must not rest solely on automated processing and becomes high-risk under the EU AI Act from December 2027, so the model sorts and summarises and the person decides.

in_practice.trigger: A candidate applies or is added to a vacancy in Recruitee.
steps: Read CV and form answers into fields: licences, certificates, availability, languages, work permit
Compare fields with the vacancy's hard requirements and mark met, missing or unclear
Write a three-line summary with the evidence quoted from the CV
Administrator confirms referral or rejection in Recruitee
Referred candidates go to the hiring manager in Teams with the summary
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator confirms every referral and every rejection; no stage change happens without them.
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee candidate timeline with the extracted fields, the check result and who decided.

evidence.claim: Screening applicants is listed as high-risk under Annex III 4(a) of the EU AI Act, applying from 2 December 2027.
A decision on an applicant cannot rest solely on automated processing.
Applicant tracking systems such as Recruitee hold pipeline stages and application questions that can carry knock-out fields.

risks: Model misses or invents a certificate, wrongly excluding a good candidate
Bias against non-standard CVs, for example from candidates with foreign qualifications
Works council consent needed if candidate data processing changes (WOR art. 27)
High-risk obligations from December 2027 if the tool ranks or filters applicants
research_questions: What share of warehouse and driver applicants are rejected on hard requirements alone, and how long do they wait today?
How accurate is extraction of licences and certificates from the CVs Noordhaven actually receives?
Does Recruitee's own screening question feature already cover most knock-outs without a model?
Would site leads accept a same-day referral flow, or is their review the real bottleneck?

tasks.short: Send applicants the yes or no after a decision, by email or phone.

today.trigger: A recruiter or hiring manager decides on a candidate and the stage changes in Recruitee.
steps: Check in Recruitee which candidates have a decision but no message
Pick a template and adjust it for name, role and stage
Add a personal line for interviewed candidates from the interview notes
Send by email, or call candidates who interviewed on site
Update the stage and note in Recruitee
drudgery: Copying names and roles into the same rejection template
Remembering who still has not heard anything
today.time_sinks: Interviewed candidates who deserve a personal reason; messages pile up when managers decide late.

lenses.faster: Early-stage rejections go out from templates on stage change, and for interviewed candidates a draft with a short reason taken from the interview feedback waits for one click; about 60% of the time disappears.
lenses.autonomous: The stage change in Recruitee triggers the message; early-stage rejections send after a set delay, interviewed candidates get a draft the administrator approves.
lenses.ambitious: A group served for the first time: every interviewed candidate, including those for night shifts and flex-to-permanent roles, gets a specific reason and an offer to join the talent pool, so silver candidates can be recalled in the next peak season; demand would grow because recruiters would reuse the pool.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses filling templates or finding forgotten candidates; the administrator wants more time for the phone calls to finalists.
lenses.options: Two drafts with different tone for a finalist rejection can help, but the decision itself does not change.
lenses.altitude: The administrator moves from sending letters to owning the message set and the talent pool follow-up; slightly more expert in candidate experience.
reach: Recruiter: talent pool re-engagement campaigns before peak season; needs Recruitee campaign features and labour market knowledge

tasks.human_edge: Calling a finalist with bad news, handling an upset candidate, and spotting when a written reason would be unwise or legally risky.
tasks.pattern_why: The workflow is fixed by the Recruitee stage; one model call turns interview feedback into a short, checkable reason in the template.

in_practice.trigger: A candidate moves to 'Rejected' or 'Hired' in Recruitee.
steps: Early-stage rejection: template email sends after 24 hours unless stopped
Interviewed candidate: model drafts a reason from structured interview feedback, in Dutch or English
Draft is checked against a blocklist of topics (health, age, pregnancy, origin)
Administrator approves or edits and sends from Recruitee
Offer to stay in the talent pool is recorded with consent date
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator approves every message to an interviewed candidate; early-stage templates run without review.
data_needed: Approved templates per stage and language
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee candidate timeline with the sent message and approver.

evidence.claim: The acceptance or rejection letter can be automated; the decision itself cannot rest solely on automated processing.
AI summaries of interviews create a paper trail that may include unlawful or sensitive content.
Recruitee supports email templates triggered by pipeline stages.

risks: A generated reason reveals a discriminatory or sensitive ground taken from interview notes
A message sent before the manager's decision is final
Talent pool data kept longer than consent allows under AVG
research_questions: How many candidates per month never receive a message or wait more than a week?
Is interview feedback in Recruitee structured enough to draft a fair reason?
Do candidates who get a specific reason reapply or accept a later offer more often?

tasks.short: Handle pension, bike plan, CAO allowances and insurance questions and changes for employees.

today.trigger: An employee emails or calls about pension, travel allowance, bike scheme, a CAO allowance or the absence insurance, or a life event needs a change.
steps: Read the question and look up the employee's contract and CAO in AFAS
Find the rule in the CAO, the scheme document or the pension fund site
Answer by email or phone, or fill the change form
Enter the mutation in AFAS and send a check to payroll
Pass anything medical or disputed to the HR Business Partner
drudgery: Answering the same travel allowance and bike scheme questions
Looking up which CAO applies to which person
today.time_sinks: Two CAOs with different rules, questions by phone from shift workers, and follow-up with payroll on mutations.

lenses.faster: Personal entitlements come from a deterministic AFAS lookup, policy questions are answered from owned CAO and scheme content, and change requests arrive pre-filled; the administrator handles exceptions and approves mutations, saving about a third.
lenses.autonomous: A question in Teams or an AFAS form starts it; standard answers go out quoting the lookup and source, change requests wait for the administrator's approval before entry in AFAS.
lenses.ambitious: A group served for the first time: warehouse and transport staff on night and weekend shifts in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get an answer on their own entitlements outside office hours instead of calling during a break; demand would grow because many questions are never asked today.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the tenth travel allowance question of the week; the administrator wants more time for life events like a birth, divorce or death where people need a person.
lenses.options: Scenarios matter when an employee chooses, for example extra pension savings or the bike scheme: showing two or three net-pay outcomes changes the choice.
lenses.altitude: The administrator becomes owner of the benefits knowledge base and the exception queue, with the right to publish answers within approved content; the job becomes more expert in CAO and scheme rules.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: maintaining scheme documentation and annual enrolment communications; needs scheme and tax (werkkostenregeling) knowledge
Payroll Specialist: first check of benefit mutations before month close; needs AFAS payroll components

tasks.human_edge: Life events and disputes, anything touching health or incapacity (WIA, verzuim insurance), and judging when a question is really a complaint or a sign of trouble.
tasks.pattern_why: Questions vary and the path to an answer cannot be fixed in advance, so an agent works on owned content with a deterministic entitlement lookup and escalates; changes need a person's approval before they count.

in_practice.trigger: An employee asks a question in Teams or the AFAS portal, or submits a change request.
steps: Identify the employee and their CAO and contract from AFAS
Quote personal entitlements from a deterministic lookup, never generated
Answer policy questions from approved CAO and scheme content with the source named
Open a ticket with the profile attached when unsure or when health is mentioned
Administrator approves change requests before the mutation is entered in AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: Every mutation in AFAS and every escalated question is handled by the administrator; the bot discloses it is AI.
data_needed: Contract, CAO and scheme participation per employee
CAO texts and scheme documents with a named owner
in_practice.logs_to: Ticket queue in AFAS workflow or the HR mailbox, with question, answer source and approver; question logs per employee only with works council consent.

evidence.claim: Coca-Cola Andina's HR agent answers per region, contract type and tenure and turns unresolved questions into tickets with the profile attached; 1,200 of 3,600 employees use it monthly, CSAT 4.1.
A chatbot alone saved about 3% of work hours; hours come from redesigned workflows.
SAP Joule HR agents answer or dispatch HR questions and explain payslips.
A bot answering from the personnel file needs works council consent under WOR art. 27(1)(k).
Employee-facing bots must disclose they are AI (Art. 50(1)).

risks: Wrong entitlement stated if generated rather than looked up
Health data entering prompts (GDPR Art. 9)
Tone failures on sensitive topics, as Andina found before launch
Works council consent delays launch
research_questions: What share of benefit contacts are repeat policy questions versus personal changes?
Can AFAS expose entitlements per employee reliably for a lookup?
Will shift workers use Teams on their phones, or is sign-in the barrier as at Andina?
Will the works council consent to logging questions per employee?

tasks.short: Post vacancies on job boards and intranet and tell eligible employees about internal openings.

today.trigger: A recruiter or manager approves a new vacancy.
steps: Copy the function description from SharePoint into a vacancy text
Publish via Recruitee to job boards and the careers page
Post on the intranet and Teams channels per site
Email employees who might qualify, found by asking site leads
Order agency workers through the agency portal if the role is flex
drudgery: Rewriting the same function description into ad text
Guessing which employees qualify for an internal opening
today.time_sinks: Writing texts per channel and language, and finding eligible internal candidates without a skills overview.

lenses.faster: The vacancy text is drafted from the function description and CAO scale per channel, and eligible internal employees are found by a query on AFAS function and Studytube certificates; the administrator checks and publishes, saving about 45%.
lenses.autonomous: Vacancy approval in Recruitee triggers the draft texts and the eligible-employee list; the administrator approves texts and the notification list before anything goes out.
lenses.ambitious: A group served for the first time: flex workers on long assignments who hold the right certificates are told about permanent openings, turning the flex pool into a hiring source with people already productive on day one; demand would grow because it feeds the North Star directly.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses reformatting ad text for four channels; the administrator wants more time on talking with internal candidates about a move.
lenses.options: Two or three ad variants (for example emphasising shift pay versus fixed hours) can be tested per channel, and the results change which text the recruiter keeps.
lenses.altitude: The administrator runs internal mobility notices and owns which employees and flex workers are told about which roles; more expert in the labour market of the three regions.
reach: Recruiter: writing and channel choice for vacancy ads; needs labour market and employer branding basics
L&D Specialist: linking certificate gaps to internal candidates; needs Studytube reporting

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether internal posting comes first under the CAO and fairness rules, and knowing which flex worker or employee the site lead really rates.
tasks.pattern_why: A fixed workflow with one model call to turn the function description into channel texts; the eligibility list is a plain query.

in_practice.trigger: A vacancy is approved in Recruitee.
steps: Draft ad texts per channel from function description, CAO scale and site
Query AFAS and Studytube for employees with the function family and valid certificates
Add flex workers on assignment longer than a set period, from agency portal data
Administrator approves texts and list
Publish via Recruitee and send internal notices in Teams and email
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator approves every ad text and the internal notification list.
data_needed: Certificates and validity dates from Studytube
Flex worker assignment lists from agencies
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee vacancy record with texts, channels and the list of people notified.

evidence.claim: Recruitee publishes vacancies to multiple job boards from one record.
Allocating tasks or monitoring performance is high-risk from December 2027; a notice of openings based on certificates is not a selection decision but should not rank people.

risks: Agency contracts may restrict direct recruitment of flex workers or charge a takeover fee
Notifying some employees and not others feels unfair if the rule is unclear
Studytube certificate data incomplete for older staff
research_questions: What do the three agency contracts say about taking over flex workers?
How many hires in the last year came from internal or flex candidates, and how did their 90-day retention compare?
Is Studytube certificate data complete enough to drive the list?

tasks.short: Look up employee data for mortgage forms, bailiffs, UWV and reference requests, after checking they are authorised.

today.trigger: An employee asks for a werkgeversverklaring for a mortgage, or a bailiff, UWV, pension fund or bank sends a request.
steps: Check who is asking and whether there is consent or a legal basis
Look up contract, salary and employment dates in AFAS
Fill the lender's or authority's form, often a PDF
Get a signature from an authorised signatory
Send securely and file a copy in the digital dossier
drudgery: Retyping the same salary and contract fields into different PDF forms
today.time_sinks: Many different form layouts, urgent mortgage deadlines, and checking garnishment calculations.

lenses.faster: The request is classified and the form filled from AFAS fields automatically, so the administrator checks authorisation and figures and signs off; about 55% of the time goes.
lenses.autonomous: An incoming request in the HR mailbox triggers classification and form filling; nothing leaves the building until the administrator has confirmed the authorisation and the content.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to employees: a werkgeversverklaring ready within one working day through the AFAS portal, which helps employees who are buying a house in a tight market; demand would grow somewhat as people stop asking for informal salary letters instead.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping salary data into bank PDFs; the administrator keeps the judgement on unusual requests and garnishment cases.
lenses.options: Not applicable; the output is a factual statement with one correct content.
lenses.altitude: The administrator becomes the gatekeeper for data leaving the company, with the right to refuse requests without a basis; slightly more expert in AVG and garnishment rules.
reach: Payroll Specialist: processing wage garnishments (loonbeslag) and the beslagvrije voet; needs garnishment law and AFAS payroll

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a requester is authorised and whether a request is genuine, refusing when there is no basis, and handling garnishment with care for the employee.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call reads the incoming letter or form into a request type and fields; the data comes from AFAS by fixed rules and a person approves.

in_practice.trigger: A request arrives in the HR mailbox or an employee submits a form in AFAS.
steps: Classify request type and requester and extract the fields asked for
Check against a register of allowed requesters and required consent
Fill the form from AFAS data, no generated figures
Administrator verifies authorisation and figures and signs or routes to signatory
Send securely and file in the AFAS dossier
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator approves every outgoing disclosure.
data_needed: Contract, salary and employment history in AFAS
Register of request types and legal bases
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS digital dossier with the request, basis, data sent and approver.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8's Jonas reads documents into dossier fields.
Disclosing personal data needs a legal basis under the GDPR; document intake is best done as document-to-fields plus deterministic validation with an exceptions queue.

risks: Data sent to an unauthorised or fake requester (phishing)
Wrong salary figure on a mortgage statement
Personal data sent to a model outside the EU without a processing agreement
research_questions: How many requests per month and of which types reach HR?
Can Jonas in AFAS Profit 8 read incoming request letters well enough?
Do the main Dutch lenders accept a standard werkgeversverklaring generated from AFAS?

tasks.short: Make the monthly headcount, absence, flex and mutation reports for management and the works council.

today.trigger: Month end, a management meeting, or a works council request.
steps: Export data from AFAS and Power BI into Excel
Add flex worker counts from the three agency portals
Clean and combine the sheets, check against last month
Write a short commentary and build the slides
Send to the HR Director, site managers or works council
drudgery: Merging three agency exports with different formats
Rebuilding the same tables each month
today.time_sinks: Flex data outside AFAS and manual checks for differences with last month.

lenses.faster: Agency data is loaded automatically next to the AFAS extract, the standard report is built in Power BI, and a short commentary is drafted for review; about 60% of the time goes.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly refresh and month-end calendar produce the report; the administrator reviews outliers and the commentary before it is sent.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get a weekly view of week-one onboarding, flex share and 90-day leavers per shift, so they act on early leavers within the week instead of at quarter end; demand would grow as managers ask for it.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses copying agency exports into Excel; the administrator wants more time on explaining what the numbers mean to managers.
lenses.options: Little; the numbers are fixed, though choosing which three trends to highlight is a judgement.
lenses.altitude: The administrator owns the standard report set and its definitions, and spends time on the conversation with site managers; more expert in data.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: maintaining standard Power BI reports and data definitions; needs Power BI and AFAS data model skills
FP&A Analyst: flex labour cost reporting per site; needs agency invoice data

tasks.human_edge: Knowing why a number moved (a reorganisation, a peak, a mis-keyed mutation) and what not to show, such as small groups where individuals can be identified.
tasks.pattern_why: Definitions and calculations can be written down; build the pipeline and report once and run it without a model, with an optional one-call commentary draft.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly calendar date and the nightly AFAS refresh; weekly for site views.
steps: Load agency hours and headcount files into the same model as the AFAS extract
Compute standard measures with fixed definitions
Flag differences above a threshold against last period
Suppress groups smaller than a set size
Administrator reviews flags and commentary and publishes
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator reviews flagged outliers and the commentary before release; the works council version is approved by the HR Director.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI workspace version history and a SharePoint archive of published reports.

evidence.claim: Power BI can combine an AFAS extract with other files on a scheduled refresh.

risks: Absence figures per small team reveal health information about individuals
Agency file formats change without notice
Generated commentary states a cause that is not true
research_questions: How many hours per month go into the current reports, split by gathering versus writing?
Can the three agencies deliver data in a fixed format or through an API?
Would site managers use a weekly view, and what would they do differently?

tasks.short: Keep org charts, the staff handbook, directories and evaluation forms up to date.

today.trigger: A new CAO, a policy change, a reorganisation, or a quarterly check.
steps: Collect changes from AFAS mutations, managers and new CAO texts
Edit the handbook and forms in Word on SharePoint
Redraw org charts in Visio or PowerPoint
Get approval from the HR Director, and works council consent where a regulation changes
Publish and tell staff
drudgery: Redrawing org charts by hand after each mutation
Finding every place in the handbook a CAO change touches
today.time_sinks: Tracking CAO changes through the handbook and waiting for approvals.

lenses.faster: Org charts and directories are generated from AFAS, and a new CAO text is compared with the handbook to produce a marked-up draft of the passages to change; the administrator reviews and routes for approval, saving about 45%.
lenses.autonomous: An AFAS mutation regenerates the org chart; a new CAO or policy triggers the comparison draft, which waits for review and approval.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the HR bot and every employee: the handbook kept as structured, owned content per topic that answers shift workers' questions accurately, because the Andina case shows content structure decides answer quality; demand would grow with bot use.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses redrawing boxes in Visio; the administrator wants more time on writing clear policy text people actually read.
lenses.options: Two wordings of a changed rule can help the HR Director and works council choose, which changes what is agreed.
lenses.altitude: The administrator becomes the named owner of the HR knowledge base used by people and the bot, deciding structure and wording within approved policy; the job becomes more expert.
reach: HR Business Partner: drafting policy changes for works council consultation; needs WOR procedure knowledge
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: org structure data in AFAS; needs AFAS organisation module

tasks.human_edge: Interpreting what a CAO change means in practice at Noordhaven, knowing what the works council must see, and writing so warehouse staff understand it.
tasks.pattern_why: Org charts are deterministic from AFAS; the handbook update is one model call comparing new rules with existing text, inside a fixed approval workflow.

in_practice.trigger: An AFAS organisation mutation, a new CAO text, or a policy decision.
steps: Regenerate org charts and directories from AFAS
Compare new CAO or policy text with the handbook and mark affected passages
Draft replacement text with the source clause cited
Administrator reviews; HR Director approves; works council consent where WOR art. 27 applies
Publish on SharePoint and update the bot's content
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator reviews every draft change and the HR Director approves publication.
data_needed: New CAO texts and policy decisions
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history with approver and source clause per change.

evidence.claim: SixFifty drafts handbooks and contracts grounded in an attorney-maintained law base and strict workflows (US law only).
Content structure mattered more than expected for the HR bot; a named owner per region writes the knowledge.
Changes to certain regulations need works council consent under WOR art. 27.

risks: A missed CAO change leaves the handbook wrong and the bot repeating it
Draft text published without works council consent
Org chart shows personal data more widely than needed
research_questions: How far behind the current CAOs is the handbook today?
Can AFAS export organisation structure cleanly enough for automatic charts?
Which handbook sections need works council consent when they change?

role.altitude: The HR Administrator moves from keying, copying and answering the same questions to owning the HR knowledge base, the requirement profiles and the exception queues, with the right to publish approved answers and to refuse data requests without a basis; the job becomes more expert in CAO rules, AVG and data.
reach: Recruiter: first screening and talent pool follow-up for warehouse and driver roles
Payroll Specialist: first check of benefit mutations and garnishments before month close
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: maintaining standard reports and measure definitions in Power BI
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: scheme documentation and enrolment communications
L&D Specialist: certificate gap lists for internal candidates
role.ceiling_note: Of these seven tasks (about 27% of the role, roughly 850 hours a year across 2 FTE) about 45% of the time can go, around 380 hours or EUR 18,000 a year; the limit is decisions about people, health data, works council consent and disclosures that must stay with a person.
skills_to_grow: Writing and structuring policy content for people and a bot
AVG and EU AI Act basics for HR
Power BI and AFAS data model
role.ambitious_version: The administrator runs an HR service that answers every employee, including night-shift staff and long-term flex workers on all three sites, the same day, turns flex workers with valid certificates into permanent hires, and gives site managers a weekly view of early leavers so the 90-day North Star moves.
